proposals.relationship: With Artibise, credits Careless’s metropolitan and national perspectives with helping establish Canadian urban history.
proposals.evidence_note: The jointly authored1984 report p6 explicitly treats Careless’s1954 and1968 articles as part of the field’s self-conscious beginning. Davis1985 p96/n3 independently quotes that assessment. This is a particular historiographical resource/recognition, not exclusive descent, formal mentoring or agreement with every metropolitan thesis. Artibise retains coauthorship. Report text was read through selected indexed primary passages; full PDF inaccessible.

proposals.relationship: With Artibise, uses Creighton’s account of commercial elites and metropolitan power in reconstructing the history of Canadian urban interpretation.
proposals.evidence_note: Their own report p6 explains Creighton’s account of Montreal businessmen and the urban network, citing The Commercial Empire of the St. Lawrence in note20. This is bounded analytical use in a joint historiographical survey, not a claim Linteau endorses the interpretation or adopted it unchanged in his Montreal books. Innis/Lower are also credited as predecessors; their work is not collapsed into Creighton’s. Original Creighton book remains unread.

proposals.relationship: Places Linteau’s economic history within a qualified criticism of nationally framed explanations and revisions of the French-Canadian bourgeoisie thesis.
proposals.evidence_note: Ouellet1985 p18 criticizes the dominant national-inferiority preoccupation and explicitly cites Durocher/Linteau’s1971 anthology. On19–20 he locates Robert/Linteau/Normand Séguin within revisions of Maurice Séguin’s thesis and identifies Maisonneuve and joint landownership studies. This decomposes the existing named group route990 with its qualifications: not a charge that Linteau accepts Séguin unchanged, rejects all ethnic factors, or shares every view later assigned to Bourque/Sales. Linteau1976 expressly gives ethnicity a secondary role; positions are attributed rather than adjudicated.
